item.name: Queue a manual AI damage scan for an inspection

request.name: Queue a manual AI damage scan for an inspection

description.content:
Enqueues a manual AI damage-detection scan against a completed inspection
and returns the throttle record clients poll for progress.

Guards enforced before enqueue:
  - Caller must be on an active Pro Plan (returns 404 `subscription not found`
    when no subscription record exists, otherwise 403 with the
    Pro-Plan-required message).
  - The account must have manual AI damage detection enabled.
  - The inspection must exist, be completed, and have inspection metadata.
  - The inspection must not already have a previous scan.
  - The caller must have manual-scan permissions and access to the
    inspection.

response.name: Returns the queued throttle record.

description.content:
Removes the current performer (renter) from the inspection and records a removal reason. This is
used by the mobile flow when a resident is moving out or a duplicate invite needs to be
cleaned up. Returns 204 with no content on success.

Note: this `DELETE /v1/inspections/{inspectionId}` route is distinct from the bulk
`DELETE /v1/inspections?id[]=...` endpoint, which deletes inspections by id.

response.name: Renter successfully removed.

  - `only renters are allowed to perform this action`

Claims a pending additional-signature request from a Branch deep link,
reassigning `recipient_email` to the authenticated caller. The linked
request and every other pending additional-signature request addressed to
the original recipient's email are reassigned to the caller.

Possession of the high-entropy request id is treated as the capability to
claim the request (the deep link acts as a bearer token), so — unlike the
GET endpoint — this endpoint does not require the caller's email to match
the request's recipient. Returns the affected requests so the apps can
surface the newly-claimed inspections.

description.content:
Zapier-flavoured entry point for the v2 inspection create flow. The
Zapier request body carries a flat inspection payload; the property is
resolved by (`address` + `postal_code`) within the caller's user +
organizations — matched against the resolved inspection template's
`property_type` — then the up-to-five `resident_email_N` fields are
translated into the v2 `recipients` shape (`{ type: 'emails', emails }`
when any resident email is provided, otherwise `{ type: 'self-perform' }`)
and delegated to the v2 create flow.

response.name:
Returns the standard v2 create envelope — an array of successful
inspections plus per-property error / warning / conflict payloads.
Individual property-level failures do not surface as 4xx; they are
recorded in `errors[].reason` on the 200 response.

info.name: RentCheck REST Account Settings Inspections API

description.content:
## Mission
At RentCheck, our mission is plain and simple: To make renting fair and transparent for everyone involved. 
RentCheck is a property inspection solution that helps property managers save time and resources with easy self-guided inspections that residents can perform from their smartphone. 

With RentCheck, property managers can avoid tenant coordination, eliminate drive time, and standardize their inspection process. 
We provides real-time visibility to property managers and owners while bringing transparency to the security deposit deduction process.

## API
The RentCheck API lets developers tap into the RentCheck ecosystem, building their own RentCheck-powered applications to enable inspection scheduling and creation and to leverage inspection data for a variety of use cases in the property management, maintenance, and insurance spaces.

The RentCheck REST API supports JSON requests and responses and features a resource-oriented design that generally adheres to the RFC 7321 HTTP/1.1 standard. 
Our API resources provide access to many RentCheck features, including units, buildings, communities, inspections, and residents.

## Credentials
In addition to the Bearer Auth, RentCheck will need to send you an application ID and secret. These are required to generate the required application headers (x-app-id & x-app-secret).
These values can be obtained from the [RentCheck API integration page](https://app.getrentcheck.com/account/integrations/rentcheck-api).

## Rate Limiting
The RentCheck API enforces rate limits to ensure fair usage and prevent abuse. The rate limits are as follows:
- **Requests per second**: 8
- **Requests per minute**: 256
- **Requests per 10 minutes**: 1024

If you exceed the rate limits, you will receive a 429 Too Many Requests response.

## Pagination
When interacting with endpoints that return a list of items, the results are paginated to help manage large data sets efficiently. The following parameters control pagination:
- **page_size** (integer): Defines the number of items returned per page. The maximum allowed value is 250. If a value larger than 250 is provided, it will be automatically clamped to 250. This ensures that the system performs optimally and prevents the server from being overwhelmed by too many items in a single response.
  - **Maximum**: `250`
- **page_number** (integer): Indicates the page number to retrieve. Pagination starts at `page 0`. If not specified, the first page (`page 0`) is returned by default.
### Example Request
```http
GET /api/v1/inspections?page_size=300&page_number=2
```
In this example, although the `page_size` parameter is set to `300` **for a query with 1500 total results**, the system will return only `250` items per page, as `300` exceeds the maximum allowed value.
#### Example Response
```json
{
    "status": 200,
    "data": [...],
    "count": 250,
    "total_results": 1500
}
```
This response shows that the `page_size` has been clamped to `250`, despite the initial request for `300`.
